records.real_world_identity_notes: PMR's Storm GT name resolves to the late-period Lister Storm GT/GTM competition family represented by the existing record. The 2000-onward Storm GT is the six-speed sequential version: the 2000 championship car is described both as Storm GT and as chassis GTM 002. The earlier 1999 homologation documents a different six-speed Getrag manual/synchromesh configuration and must not be silently inherited by the late-period record.
records.confidence_basis: The official PMR page names Lister Storm GT. A documented 2000 Lister championship car explicitly says the Storm GT used from 2000 onward had a six-speed sequential gearbox and identifies its chassis as GTM 002; it also calls the car a 2000 Lister Storm GTM. This provides the independent bridge from PMR's abbreviated display name to the existing GTM record. FIA Form GT-008 is retained as an adjacent-variant warning because its 1999 base homologation lists a Getrag six-speed manual with synchronisers.

records.specification_basis: Both the 2000-onward sequential specification and the earlier FIA homologation list six forward ratios. For the late-period record resolved here, the documented 2000 Storm GT/GTM uses a Hewland TGTA six-speed sequential. The 1999 Getrag manual is explicitly treated as an earlier adjacent variant. The exact 2000 specification states a push-pull lever, and the documented 2003-spec cockpit photograph visibly shows a tall lever beside the driver. No reviewed exact-car source supports paddles for this late-period car. The 2000-onward specification explicitly calls the gearbox sequential and describes the push-pull lever. Manual blip is a downshift action in this data model; no upshift-blip procedure is asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this data model; the reviewed real-car sources do not describe an upshift blip. Throttle lift is recorded as an upshift action in this data model; no separate downshift-lift claim is made. No downshift cut is established; the source is silent on such a function. The clear cockpit photograph of a Storm GT returned to its 2003 appearance shows a continuous circular rim with a central button hub, not a flattened D rim or fixed-grip gt-formula face. The photographed rim is continuous across the upper section; no upper opening is visible. This is evidence for the photographed 2003-spec restoration, not every earlier Storm variant. The wheel has a button hub but no integrated readout; the visible display is mounted in the dashboard behind the rim. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.

records.driver_summary: 6-speed lever sequential. Use the clutch to pull away. Stay flat on the upshift because the car cuts for you. Blip each downshift. The downshift blip is not established, so that much is the cautious default rather than this car's known technique. Simulator implementations differ on manual downshift blip, automatic downshift blip; follow the selected game's USE row for those items.
